I’ve been farming these 6 mu for 40 years, since I was a young man of 24. Never went to school, but the land taught me everything I need to know. It’s just me and my wife now — the children left for the city years ago — so we work these fields with our own hands, plus a few days of hired help at harvest when the weather window is tight. Money is always tight. I can’t afford to experiment or buy the fancy inputs, so I mostly do what I’ve always done, and what the other old farmers in the village do.

**Wheat (6 mu)**

I plant winter wheat on all 6 mu every year — it’s our main crop, the one that feeds us and brings cash. This year I’ll sow around October 10th, same as always. I saved most of the seed from last year’s harvest, but I bought a little fresh seed from the village shop to mix in so the vigor stays good. That costs me about 35 yuan per mu. 

For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — about 50 kg per mu. That gives the wheat a base to grow on. Then in the spring, when the wheat turns green around late March, if it looks a little yellow I topdress with another half-bag of urea, about 20 kg per mu. Last year I tried cutting back on the topdress and the yield was lower, so this year I won’t skip it. Better to spend a little more than to lose too much grain. I irrigate three times: once when the wheat turns green in March, once at jointing in April, and once at grain filling in May. Each time the electricity for pumping costs about 15 yuan per mu, but I have to do it — the well water is the only reason we can grow wheat here. I spray herbicide once in the spring to keep the weeds down, about 15 yuan per mu. I don’t use insecticide on wheat unless I see aphids, which I didn’t last year, so I won’t plan for it.

Me and my wife do all the planting, fertilizing, and spraying ourselves — about 18 days of our own labor across the season. For harvest in early June, I hire 3 days of labor because we’re old and can’t cut and carry fast enough before the weather turns.

I got about 400 kg per mu last year. The soil looks about the same this year, no big floods or droughts, so I expect about 400 kg per mu again. I’d be happy with 420, but I won’t count on it.

**Maize (6 mu)**

Right after we harvest the wheat in early June, I plant summer maize on the same 6 mu. The window is very tight — sometimes only 3 or 4 days between wheat coming out and maize going in. I don’t do deep plowing for maize; I just run the light harrow over the stubble and plant. If I took time to till properly, I might miss the planting window, and late maize never yields well.

I buy hybrid maize seed every year — you can’t save hybrid seed, everyone knows that. I need about 2.5 kg per mu, and it costs about 55 yuan per mu from the seed dealer. At planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, about 50 kg. Then at the big trumpet stage in late July or early August, I topdress with about 15 kg of urea per mu. Some years I skip the topdress if the maize looks dark green, but last year I skipped it and the yield was poor, so this year I’ll put it down for sure. Better safe than sorry.

I irrigate twice: once right after planting if it hasn’t rained, and once at flowering in August. Each irrigation costs about 15 yuan per mu. I spray herbicide once at planting to keep the weeds down, and I keep a bottle of insecticide ready because the corn borers sometimes come in August. If I see them, I spray. That’s about 25 yuan per mu for chemicals.

My wife and I do the planting and field work — about 15 family days. I hire 2 days of labor for harvest in late September because carrying the cobs is hard on our backs now.

Last year I got about 450 kg per mu on the maize. The weather has been normal so far, so I’ll expect 450 kg per mu again.

**Why I’m doing it this way**

I don’t have much cash, so I use saved wheat seed and only buy what I must — hybrid maize seed and fertilizer. I’d rather apply a little more fertilizer than too little, because a bad year hurts more than a good year helps, and at my age I can’t afford a big loss. The biggest constraint is labor — it’s just two of us, so we work slowly and hire help only when we must. The double-cropping system is hard on old bodies, but it’s the only way to get two crops off 6 mu and have enough to eat and a little to sell.
